name: Perez-Marrero DMSO
question: Does intravesical dimethyl sulfoxide improve symptoms and objective measures more than saline in patients with interstitial cystitis?

design.population: Thirty women and three men with biopsies suggestive of interstitial cystitis were enrolled; mean age was 48 years and mean symptom duration was 5.5 years.

verdictNote: Both reported improvement rates favored DMSO; trial-defined significance could not be assessed.
takeaway: In a randomized crossover trial of intravesical 50% dimethyl sulfoxide versus saline for interstitial cystitis, markedly improved symptoms were reported in 53% versus 18%, and objective improvement in 93% versus 35%.

reports.label: Controlled crossover comparison
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation, July 1988; day not reported
reports.citation: Perez-Marrero R, Emerson LE, Feltis JT. "A Controlled Study of Dimethyl Sulfoxide in Interstitial Cystitis." *J Urol.* 1988;140(1):36-39. doi:10.1016/s0022-5347(17)41478-9
reports.followUp: Assessment after intravesical treatment; timing not stated in the abstract.

results.measure: Patients markedly improved by subjective assessment; percentage of treated patients
results.note: The abstract gives percentages without arm denominators, a prespecified endpoint hierarchy, or a P value.

results.measure: Objective improvement by urodynamic assessment; percentage of treated patients
results.note: The abstract gives percentages without arm denominators, an exact objective-response definition, or a P value.

harms.label: Significant side effects from DMSO
harms.note: The abstract does not give adverse-event categories, counts, or saline-arm rates.

delivery.label: Instillation schedule
delivery.value: 50% dimethyl sulfoxide or saline intravesically every two weeks for two sessions of four treatments each, with crossover.
